axis: swelling something past its true size → planting an outright falsehood in a believer

members.tone: Names the act by its result — the untruth has landed and is believed — where *mislead* stops at the information handed over.
The same planting of a false belief, but the word frames it as a breach of the trust that made the believing possible, which is what makes it the heaviest term here.
Flat and unsoftened, covering both the untruth spoken and the pretence behind it, with no room left for an innocent reading.
The gentlest of the deceptions: it charges only the false or misleading information given and leaves intent unsettled, where *lie* settles it.
Makes the thing itself loom larger, so the overreach shows in the size of the picture rather than in a claim stated outright.
The plain charge of overstatement, taking in both going past reasonable bounds and going past the truth, and always implying the real measure is smaller.
Says only that something has been swelled; the fault lies in the going beyond, not in the verb, which is why it accuses least of the three.
